description: A junior Computer Science major focusing on cybersecurity who is confident in high-level data structures but feels anxious about low-level memory management and debugging in C.

nodes.title: Foundations: C Programming for Systems
nodes.description: Review of C-language pointers, memory addressing, and data structures necessary for kernel-level programming.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As the student has some_prior_exposure, this scaffolding node ensures their C programming skills are bridgeable to OS-specific abstractions in block_01.
This core content is required for all students; some_prior_exposure allows the student to grasp the distinction between user and kernel mode more rapidly.
nodes.description: Introduction to OS services, dual-mode operation (user vs. kernel), and system call interfaces.
nodes.title: OS Structures and Kernel Modes

nodes.description: A targeted review of the memory layout of a process (stack, heap, text) and the PCB (Process Control Block).
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with some_prior_exposure, a quick catch-up on process state transitions provides the necessary foundation for block_02 topics.
nodes.title: Process Abstraction & Life Cycle

nodes.personalizationRationale: IPC is a foundational requirement in block_02 that builds on the student's existing some_prior_exposure to basic programming.
nodes.description: Implementation of Inter-Process Communication using shared memory and message passing (sockets/pipes).
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication Mechanisms

nodes.description: Overview of multithreading models (Many-to-One, One-to-One) and the Pthreads library.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Multithreading is a core requirement; students with some_prior_exposure likely know basic threads but need the OS-level model details provided here.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries
CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.description: Analysis of scheduling criteria (throughput, turnaround) and algorithms like SRTF and Round Robin.
nodes.personalizationRationale: CPU scheduling is a core requirement of block_03 that requires analytical modeling, building on the student's some_prior_exposure to algorithms.

nodes.description: A review and practice assessment covering Chapters 1-5 to prepare for the week-8 midterm exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment is required for all students to validate mastery of blocks 01-03 before the midterm, consistent with the some_prior_exposure profile.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Blocks 1-3
Synchronization Primitives
nodes.description: The critical-section problem and software/hardware solutions including Mutexes and Semaphores.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Process synchronization is a core requirement for block_04; students with some_prior_exposure will focus on formal primitives like semaphores.

nodes.title: Classic Synchronization Problems
nodes.personalizationRationale: Solving classic sync problems is a core block_04 requirement essential for the programming project, regardless of the student's some_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Exploring classic synchronization problems such as the Bounded-Buffer and Dining Philosophers.

nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance
nodes.description: Conditions for deadlock and the Banker's Algorithm for deadlock avoidance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Deadlock characterization is a mandatory component of block_05 that fits well with the student's some_prior_exposure to logical modeling.

nodes.description: Memory management techniques including fragmentation, paging, and page table structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Physical memory management is a core requirement in block_06; students with some_prior_exposure will study the hardware-software interface.
nodes.title: Physical Memory and Paging
Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory is a mandatory block_06 topic that is heavily tested on the final and used in projects, tailored here for the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.description: Demand paging, page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO), and the concept of thrashing.

nodes.title: I/O Systems and Interfaces
nodes.description: I/O hardware interfaces, interrupt-driven I/O, and Direct Memory Access (DMA).
nodes.personalizationRationale: I/O systems are a core requirement of block_07; some_prior_exposure helps the student understand the hardware-driver interaction.

nodes.title: File System Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: File system implementation is a mandatory core component of block_07 for all students, building on the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.description: File system structures, allocation methods (indexed, linked), and directory implementation.

nodes.title: Advanced Topics: SSD and Flash Memory
nodes.description: Exploring modern flash-based storage (SSDs) and the challenges of write-amplification and wear-leveling.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's some_prior_exposure, this enrichment node provides a modern industry perspective on storage that exceeds the floor requirements.

nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review
nodes.description: Cumulative review of all course materials (Blocks 1-7) to prepare for the final examination.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory final assessment review for all students to ensure comprehensive mastery after progressing through the some_prior_exposure pathway.
